ai.description: This small frog reaches 25–30 mm. It is brownish-grey with a distinct copper-colored snout and a dark interorbital bar. It lacks webbing between fingers and toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes annandalii* is best distinguished by the prominent, bright yellow or golden-orange patch located on the posterior side of its thighs, visible when extended.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes annandalii* inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests and tea plantations in the Eastern Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Coppersmith Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining hidden in vegetation during the day and emerging at night to forage for small insects among forest foliage.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes annandalii* undergoes direct development within terrestrial eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with females laying small clutches in vegetation.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes annandalii* is endemic to the Eastern Himalayas, primarily found in the Indian states of West Bengal and Sikkim at elevations between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Coppersmith Frog emits a rhythmic, metallic "tink-tink-tink" call, reminiscent of a hammer striking metal, heard from vegetation in high-altitude forest habitats.
